articles.headline: NHTSA opens DP26010 on Robotaxi school-zone speeding petition
articles.body: On October 9, 2026, NHTSA’s Office of Defects Investigation opened Defect Petition DP26010 after receiving a September 23 petition asking it to investigate model-year 2026 Tesla Robotaxis (Model Y and Cybercab) with the Automated Driving System engaged. The petitioner alleges the ADS exceeds posted speed limits in active school zones and supplied three video links. ODI estimates about 1,000 affected vehicles and records four incidents (one ODI complaint and three social-media reports in the petition), with no crashes, injuries, or fatalities. Opening the petition means ODI will decide whether to grant or deny a formal investigation—it is not itself a recall or Preliminary Evaluation. The petition is filed under ODI number 11766676. articles.body: On the evening of October 15, 2026, Tesla unveiled the next-generation Roadster in a livestreamed event at SpaceX's test site in McGregor, Texas. articles.headline: Ninth Circuit throws out FSD false-advertising class certification
articles.body: On October 16, 2026, a Ninth Circuit panel (Judges Gould, Bybee and Bress) vacated the orders that let California buyers sue Tesla as classes over claims that cars sold since October 2016 had the hardware for full self-driving. The panel held that too many individual questions about what each buyer saw kept the claims from proceeding as a class action. The ruling does not decide the merits, and the underlying false-advertising case before U.S. District Judge Rita Lin remains pending.

articles.headline: 2026 proxy filed; Annual Meeting set for December 3
articles.body: On October 19, 2026, Tesla filed its definitive proxy statement for the 2026 Annual Meeting, set for December 3, 2026 at 3:00 p.m. Central Time at Gigafactory Texas and online, for holders of record on October 13. The ballot carries three Tesla proposals: re-electing Elon Musk, Robyn Denholm and JB Straubel as Class I directors for three-year terms, a non-binding advisory vote on 2025 executive compensation (Musk's reported at $158,359,009,867, all stock awards), and ratifying PricewaterhouseCoopers as auditor for 2026; there is no SpaceX merger vote. The proxy also launches a Voluntary Retail Voting Program, built on an SEC staff no-action letter, that lets retail holders set a standing instruction to vote with the board on all matters or on all but contested elections and mergers, starting after this meeting.

articles.headline: Q3 2026 results: $28.0B revenue, $787M GAAP net income, $1.5B free cash flow
articles.body: On October 21, 2026 Tesla furnished its Q3 2026 Update via Form 8-K Item 2.02 and held an audio-only Q&A webcast, streamed on X (63:47 replay). Unaudited Q3 figures: total revenue $28,046M; automotive $20,560M; energy generation and storage $2,881M; services and other $4,605M. GAAP operating income $718M; GAAP net income attributable to common stockholders $787M; diluted GAAP EPS $0.22; non-GAAP net income $1,697M ($0.48 per diluted share). Operating cash flow $6,263M; capex $4,732M; free cash flow $1,531M; cash, cash equivalents and short-term investments $45,447M. Operating cash flow included a $3,991M increase in accounts payable, accrued and other liabilities and a $1,255M increase in deferred revenue. Automotive gross margin excluding regulatory credits was 18.1% (16.3% in Q2). Energy gross margin rose to 33.1% from 20.4%, which CFO Vaibhav Taneja attributed mainly to tariff refunds recognized in the quarter and warranty true-downs agreed with a vendor. Active FSD subscriptions were 1.74M, excluding free trials. On the call Taneja said over 75% of North American deliveries included a paid FSD subscription sign-up at delivery, and added that every delivered car comes with a free month of FSD. The update says Optimus production began on Fremont's high-volume lines, volume production of Tesla Semi began, Megafactory Texas began production, and Tesla produced and delivered its 10 millionth vehicle.

headline: Starship Flight 15: first upper-stage tower catch; booster lost offshore
dek: SpaceX said on X on November 19 that the booster performed a safe abort on its catch return and splashed down off Starbase, and that its teams found little debris on the Mexican beach and could not clearly link it to the flight (https://x.com/SpaceX/status/2123516375805379040).

articles.headline: Starship Flight 15: first upper-stage tower catch; booster lost offshore
articles.body: Starship Flight 15 lifted off from Starbase Pad 2 at 4:47 p.m. CT on November 13, 2026, reached orbit and deployed 26 Starlink V3 satellites. After 14 orbits and about 22.5 hours, Ship 42 returned to Starbase on November 14 and was caught by the tower arms, the first catch of a Starship upper stage. Super Heavy Booster 22 ended its boostback burn early on a low fuel mass alarm, aborted its catch, diverted to the Gulf and was destroyed by its flight termination system after the landing burn. Mexico's environmental agency Profepa said on November 17 it was collecting debris at Playa Bagdad and would ask SpaceX to take responsibility (TeslaNorth, November 19).
